Container.Name: cogwheel
Container.Overview:
Cogwheel is a DNS filter for a household. It answers every name your devices look up, drops the ones on your blocklists, and lets you give a device its own rules — one tablet on a stricter profile than the rest of the house. It is one Rust binary and one SQLite file; there is no second service to run.
BEFORE YOU START: port 53 must be free on this server. Check from the Unraid terminal with: ss -lnptu '( sport = :53 )' and expect only a header. Unraid itself runs no DNS server, but two things commonly hold the port: another DNS container on host networking (Pi-hole, AdGuard Home), and, with the VM Manager enabled, libvirt's dnsmasq on virbr0. Under host networking Cogwheel binds port 53 on every address, so anything already listening on it, on any interface, stops it starting. Stop the other resolver, or give Cogwheel its own br0 address instead.
BEFORE v0.1.0: no image has been published yet, so Apply fails at the pull until the first release. Build the image yourself and put its name in Repository; docs/QUICKSTART.md#unraid has the commands.
AFTER IT STARTS: open the WebUI, then set your router's DNS server to this server's LAN address. Set it on the ROUTER, in the DHCP settings, rather than on each device, so everything on the network is covered. On a dual-stack network set the IPv6 address too: a client that keeps an IPv6 resolver configured will bypass an IPv4-only setting entirely.
DATA: the default below is a Docker named volume called cogwheel-data, which works with no further steps because the image's data directory is owned by uid 10001 and Docker copies that ownership onto a fresh named volume. A named volume lives inside Unraid's Docker storage, though, so deleting the Docker image file (a common Unraid repair step) deletes the database with it. If you would rather keep the database in appdata, where the Appdata Backup plugin picks it up, change the Data path to /mnt/user/appdata/cogwheel and run this once from the Unraid terminal before starting the container. Whoever creates that folder, Unraid or you, it is not owned by uid 10001, which is the user Cogwheel runs as:
mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/cogwheel && chown -R 10001:10001 /mnt/user/appdata/cogwheel
UPDATES: the Docker tab's update check works against the :latest tag above. An upgrade that changes the database schema migrates it in place and leaves a copy of the previous file beside it as cogwheel.db.pre-vN, so going back to an older version means restoring that copy first — the older build refuses to open a database it does not recognise. Whether a release migrates is readable from the image before you pull it:
docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/thekozugroup/cogwheel-dns:latest --format '{{ json .Image.Config.Labels }}'
and the io.cogwheel.schema-version label is the number to compare.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Where the SQLite database lives. Leave this as the named volume cogwheel-data unless you want it in appdata — see the note about ownership in the description above.

Config.Name: Web UI bind address
Config.Description: Host socket for the web interface under host networking. Change the port here if 8080 is taken on this server, and update the WebUI link to match.

Config.Name: Upstream resolvers
Config.Description: Comma-separated. The default is cleartext, which works everywhere and is readable by your ISP. For DNS-over-TLS use, for example, tls://1.1.1.1#cloudflare-dns.com,tls://1.0.0.1#cloudflare-dns.com — the name after # is the one the certificate must match and it is required.

Config.Name: Blocking mode
Config.Description: How a blocked name is answered: null_ip (0.0.0.0 / ::), nxdomain, nodata or refused. null_ip is the default because clients handle it most predictably.

Config.Name: Query log retention (days)
Config.Description: How long the Activity page keeps per-query history. This is a record of every name every device in the house looked up, so it is worth setting deliberately. 0 stops the query log entirely; the charts and per-device counts still work, because those are counts rather than browsing history.

Config.Name: Profile
Config.Description: home is the household default. dev binds loopback on high ports and is for local hacking only.
